clue.text: Academy member holding an exhibition, perhaps

definitions.text: Academy member holding an exhibition, perhaps

parts.words: Academy member holding an exhibition, perhaps
parts.note: an exhibition is a kind of college bursary, so the 'holder' is a student awarded one, not someone staging an art show

explanation.surface: A Royal Academician is putting on an art exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: At British universities an exhibition is a minor award for academic merit; the surface wants a painter hanging a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who holds an award such as a college exhibition is a learned award-holder, a member of an academic body.

clue.text: Cat is given water in French country house

parts.note: chat is the French word for cat
eau is the French word for water

explanation.surface: A cat is given a drink of water in a house in the French countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' does double service in the clue's spirit: both pieces are French words, and the definition is a French country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a castle or large manor in rural France.

clue.text: Cat found in a pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard is also called by this name
there are sixteen of these weight units in a pound avoirdupois

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a big cat of the mountains and one sixteenth of a pound weight.

clue.text: Pacify monkey, feeding it vegetables

indicators.note: the vegetables are fed into the monkey, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: an ape is a primate, loosely a monkey
peas are green vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone calms a monkey down by giving it some vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeding it' looks like a link to the vegetables; it is the container signal, with 'it' pointing back to the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone is to calm or placate them, a synonym.

clue.text: Overweight boy's tie pulled out

indicators.note: a tie pulled out of shape has its letters rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A chubby schoolboy's necktie has been tugged loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out' rearranges the seven letters of BOYS TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective 'overweight' stands for the noun here: being too heavy is the condition of obesity.

clue.text: Have chief job in school to execute

definitions.meaning: to be the head teacher, read as two words
to put to death by cutting off the head

explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE HEAD, the first half says 'be the headteacher'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off someone's head is one way to execute a condemned prisoner.

clue.text: Hose down one's supporters

definitions.meaning: hose is an old word for leg coverings
garments that run down the legs, the body's supporters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose down' tempts as a phrase about washing with a hosepipe; 'Hose' is the garment and 'supporters' are legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings are close-fitting leg garments, traditionally called hose.

clue.text: Musical effect that's a lot more complicated

indicators.note: made more complicated, the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A musical effect is described as a lot more complicated than it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges LOT MORE; the 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremolo is a wavering repetition of a note, a recognised effect in music.

clue.text: Simon cautions about being too self-righteous

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, signalling an anagram

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Simon issues warnings about someone being smug and preachy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the thirteen letters of SIMON CAUTIONS; 'being' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sanctimonious means making a show of moral superiority, excessively self-righteous.

clue.text: One imprisoned as a murderer

parts.note: reads like a convict's description, but points to the first killer in Genesis, who slew his brother Abel; also one (I) held in a can (prison)

explanation.surface: Someone has been locked up for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the elder son of Adam is the first murderer, killing his brother Abel.

clue.text: Weapon that increases the pulse rate?

definitions.text: Weapon that increases the pulse rate?

parts.words: Weapon that increases the pulse rate?
parts.note: pulse here means peas and beans, which this toy tube fires at speed

explanation.surface: Some frightening weapon makes the heart beat faster.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulses are edible seeds such as peas; the surface wants a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's toy tube used to blow dried peas, a mock weapon.

clue.text: Information a girl found in Switzerland

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Some news about a young woman has turned up in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a city located in Switzerland, on Lake Geneva.

clue.text: Fool to pocket a ball at the end of break

indicators.note: the potting piece comes after the breaking piece

parts.note: to crack is to break
in snooker, to pot is to sink a ball into a pocket

explanation.surface: A snooker player foolishly tries to pot a ball at the end of his break.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a break is a player's run of scoring shots; here 'break' is CRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or foolish person, a crank.

clue.text: It's a shame having to eat it

definitions.text: It's a shame having to eat it

parts.words: It's a shame having to eat it
parts.note: the idiom for being forced to admit an error and be humiliated, pictured as a dish

explanation.definitionFit: To 'eat' this dish is the idiom for making a humiliating apology or climbdown.

clue.text: Animals that have to rub on trees

parts.note: to buff is to polish by rubbing
aloes are succulent plants, some tree-sized

explanation.surface: Some animals are scratching themselves against trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have to' and 'on' are links; in a down clue 'on' just means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffaloes are large wild oxen, so they are animals.

clue.text: A league match

definitions.meaning: an alliance or association of members

explanation.definitionFit: A union is both an association of bodies, like a trade league, and a marriage or pairing.

clue.text: Bar gets very loud on port in Scotland

parts.note: to bar is to ban
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A pub gets rowdy in a Scottish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a coastal town and harbour in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: He breaks down in the course of an investigation

definitions.text: He breaks down in the course of an investigation

parts.words: He breaks down in the course of an investigation
parts.note: not someone collapsing in tears, but a person who breaks matters down into parts to examine them

explanation.surface: A suspect cracks under questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst examines something in detail by separating it into its parts.

clue.text: Lucky thing, so he — or she — makes out

indicators.note: the letters are made out into a new form, an anagram

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a charm brings luck, whether to him or her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes out' rearranges the nine letters of SO HE OR SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

clue.text: View from the flats

parts.note: flats are painted wooden screens on a stage, which together make up the backdrop

explanation.surface: Someone admires the outlook from their apartment block.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre backdrops built from painted flats form the stage setting, and 'scenery' also means a landscape view.

clue.text: Gold coin replaced old South American currency

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different place

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gold coin has replaced an old Latin American currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges COIN to INOC. 'Currency' means a current, so the answer is a river, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: A currency here is a flowing current: the Orinoco is a great river of Venezuela.

clue.text: Cartoon character for father to watch

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
to eye is to watch

explanation.surface: Dad settles down to watch a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye is the spinach-eating sailor of animated cartoons.

clue.text: Dish for a Scotsman? Girl returns with one

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman

indicators.note: the girl's name is turned round

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl comes back with a meal for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a pasta dish, as in macaroni cheese.

clue.text: Movable sight screen

parts.note: suggests the white screen behind a cricket bowler, but means the flap of skin that covers the eye

explanation.surface: A portable screen at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A sightscreen is the large white board behind the bowler in cricket that helps batters see the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: This fold of skin moves to cover the eye, screening sight.

clue.text: Small part actor gets a run

definitions.meaning: a film walk-on with no lines
in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs from wides, byes and no-balls are credited to the team, not the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a background film performer and, in cricket, a run scored other than off the bat.

clue.text: Side facing a corner?

parts.note: a team facing a corner kick in football, really the longest side of a right-angled triangle, opposite the right angle

explanation.surface: A football team defends a corner kick.
explanation.definitionFit: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite the right-angle corner has this name.

clue.text: Easy pace of David Copperfield

definitions.meaning: a gentle running gait, between a walk and a canter
the nickname his aunt Betsey Trotwood gives David in Dickens's novel

explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's David Copperfield, Aunt Betsey renames David 'Trotwood' and calls him by a short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a jogging gait and also the pet name of Dickens's hero David Copperfield.

clue.text: Tess had jumble hidden away

indicators.note: jumbling the letters mixes them into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Tess hid her rummage-sale items out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumble' rearranges TESS HAD; the surface wants a jumble sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashed means stored secretly, so hidden away.

clue.text: Monday's arrangement for current suppliers

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters in a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Monday's schedule is set out for the electricity companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges MONDAYS, the possessive S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamos are generators that produce electric current.
